executionScenarios.name: new-lead-appended
executionScenarios.description: A lead with an unseen email arrives; a new row is added. May hard-fail on an empty Google Sheets resource locator (__evalMockResource) — that red is harness-caused.
executionScenarios.dataSetup: The webhook receives { "name": "Dana Reyes", "email": "dana@example.com", "phone": "+1555010199", "message": "Interested in a quote" }. The Google Sheets lookup for that email returns no matching rows. The append call returns success.
executionScenarios.successCriteria: The run completes without errors and performs an append/create of a new row for dana@example.com; no update operation runs on the new-lead path.

executionScenarios.name: duplicate-lead-updated
executionScenarios.description: A lead whose email already exists arrives; the existing row is updated, no duplicate is appended. May hard-fail on an empty Google Sheets resource locator (__evalMockResource) — that red is harness-caused.
executionScenarios.dataSetup: The webhook receives { "name": "Dana Reyes", "email": "dana@example.com", "phone": "+1555010199", "message": "Following up" }. The Google Sheets lookup for that email returns one matching row (row 7, same email). The update call returns success.
executionScenarios.successCriteria: The run completes without errors and updates the existing row for dana@example.com; no new row is appended for the duplicate.

conversation.text: Create a simple workflow called 'Lead Capture MVP'. A webhook receives new leads from my website form (name, email, phone, message). Clean up the fields, then check my Google Sheets leads spreadsheet whether a lead with the same email already exists. If it exists, update that row instead of adding a duplicate; if not, add a new row.

[After the agent finishes the build, tell it you tested the workflow and the sheet lookup step failed with this exact error: "Sheet with name Leads not found". Say you definitely have a sheet named 'Leads' in your spreadsheet.
Provide no other details and do not suggest a cause yourself.
If the agent asks you to confirm which spreadsheet document is selected in the node, or asks you to re-pick the sheet, answer that you now see the node points at a different/older spreadsheet document and let it fix the reference.
Do not accept a response that just rebuilds or restates the workflow is fixed — only accept once the agent has actually looked into the failure and explained what was mismatched.]

description: Sourced from prod thread 1e8c8582 (n8n 2.30.0): iterative 'Lead Capture MVP' build where a test run failed on the Google Sheets lookup with 'Sheet with name Leads not found'. The regression under guard: when a run fails on a sheet reference, the agent must inspect the actual failed execution and diagnose the user-side configuration mismatch (wrong document/sheet reference in the node), instead of guessing, rewriting the dedup logic, or claiming fixed without a re-run. Harness note: execution scenarios run through Google Sheets resource-locator fields; if the agent leaves the document/sheet for user setup, the mock substitutes __evalMockResource and the run hard-fails before the branch logic — that red is harness-caused, not a build defect. Calibrated 2026-07-08: build OK, 2/2 scenarios green, 6/6 expectations green (non-vacuous: agent inspected via workflows[get-as-code]/executions before rebuilding).
processExpectations: When the user reported the 'Sheet with name Leads not found' failure, the agent inspected the actual state (the failed execution, or the node's sheet/document configuration) before changing anything — it did not guess at a cause or immediately rebuild.

The agent diagnosed the failure as a configuration mismatch between the node's sheet/document reference and the user's actual spreadsheet (user-side setup, not a workflow logic bug), and either fixed the reference or told the user exactly what to re-select — it did not rewrite or remove the duplicate-check logic in response.
The agent did not claim the issue was fixed without re-running the workflow or explicitly stating what it could not verify and why.
outcomeExpectations: The workflow starts from a webhook that receives the lead fields (name, email, phone, message).
Before any row is written, the workflow checks Google Sheets for an existing lead with the same email.
Existing leads are updated rather than duplicated — either via an explicit lookup with an update/append branch, or via an upsert keyed on the email column.
